title: Python 3.15 Ships and Other Python News for November 2026
description: Python 3.15 ships, 3.16 eyes None-aware operators, eight broken CA keys trigger security releases, and Anthropic drops temperature.
summary: After an eight-day delay, Python 3.15 finally shipped on October 9, and Python 3.16’s first alpha followed only four days later. The alpha arrived alongside two new PEPs that propose bringing ?. and ?? to Python, more than ten years after the last attempt stalled.
takeaways: Release manager Hugo van Kemenade’s announcement counts 5,643 commits from 1,012 contributors since Python 3.14.
Miguel Grinberg ran his yearly benchmark, How Fast Is Python 3.15? , against the third release candidate, a few days before the final release.

He concludes: Python 3.15 is at best a fairly minor improvement over 3.14 in terms of performance. (Source) The runtime of his recursive fib(40) benchmark only dropped from 7.17 seconds on 3.14 to 6.94 seconds on 3.15, about a three-percent gain.
